prompt: Some people think that the increasing use of computers and mobile phones nowadays has unwanted effects on young people's reading and writing skills. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often claimed that the growing dependence of young people on computers and mobile phones is having a damaging effect on their ability to read and write properly. I partly agree with this view, since the impact depends largely on how these devices are actually used.

The main risk is that young people stop practising writing altogether, and any skill left unused eventually fades. Some students let artificial intelligence do their research or presentation, which can save them time at the cost of quality. A student may submit excellent essays all year, then struggle to produce a single paragraph in an examination hall. Moreover, if a student has poor writing skills they can get lower grades without artificial intelligence help. As a result, artificial intelligence can produce people who are not able to write and can damage society with uneducated people.

However, if students use artificial intelligence correctly, it would not affect the quality of their work. When writing about personal experience, for example, the technology has clear limitations, though it can still help students clarify their own ideas. Some students do not have a choice about using artificial intelligence with tight deadlines. It can help them save a significant amount of time to focus on creating new ideas or solving complex problems.

In conclusion, I partly agree that technology is harming young people's literacy. The damage comes not from the devices themselves but from students who let them do the thinking, while those who use them as a tool lose nothing.
